prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D layout of an elevated, semi-enclosed construction bay with a left wall (~0.5–1 m away), a right wall (~1.5–2.5 m away), an overhead lintel, horizontal scaffolding pipes below (~1.5–2.5 m away), and an open exterior portal looking down onto an outdoor yard. A nearby person in a maroon shirt on the left is rendered as a bright foreground silhouette within or just beyond the camera wearer's arm's reach, rising from a bent posture at ~0.8 m in frame 1 to stand upright at ~0.5–0.8 m in frame 2 (occluding the left scaffolding and portal edge), and then retreating forward along the scaffolding to ~1.5–2 m by frame 5 while facing away from the camera wearer. A second person in a yellow shirt stands outside and below the opening at ~4–5 m from the camera wearer (~3–4 m beyond and below the first person), facing toward the opening with their lower legs occluded by the sill and scaffolding, while holding an object within their own arm's reach in frames 1–2. Compared to RGB, the depth map makes the continuous distance gradient along the side walls, the step-off drop to the exterior person, and the foreground person's gradual retreat much clearer despite strong backlighting and shadows. However, the map is unreliable where it hallucinates a raised 3D surface on the lower-center scaffolding in frame 2 caused by a dark cast shadow, merges thin parallel scaffolding bars into solid strips, and clips the sunlit outdoor yard and motorcycle (~8–15 m away) into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the two people from the unlabeled construction structure across all five frames: the large foreground silhouette on the left (~0.5–2 m from the camera wearer) and the smaller mid-ground silhouette centered in the exterior opening (~4–5 m away and ~3–4 m beyond the foreground person). It tracks the foreground person rising from the lower-left corner in frame 1 to fill the left half of the view in frames 2–3 (where their head reaches the top frame edge and their legs are cropped at the bottom edge) before narrowing and shifting upward-left as they step away along the scaffolding in frames 4–5, facing away from the camera wearer throughout. The distant person's mask remains at a steady position to the right of the foreground person, showing their upper body facing the camera wearer while their legs stay occluded below the opening sill and scaffolding pipes. While segmentation cleanly separates the dimly lit foreground worker from the shadowed left wall and the distant worker from the cluttered outdoor background, it conveys no metric depth or 3D orientation on its own and completely omits the walls, scaffolding pipes within arm's reach, and handheld bricks. The map is notably unreliable in frame 4, where it mislabels the foreground person's back and legs as a 'horse', misclassifies the overhead concrete lintel as an 'umbrella', and fragments the top-left shoulder into a separate 'person' mask, as well as in frame 3 where a tiny stray mask appears near the distant motorcycle.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons for either person in the scene. From the RGB strip, the foreground person is ~0.5–2 m away on the left, within arm's reach of the camera wearer and the left wall in frames 1–3, facing away from the camera wearer toward the outdoor opening while rising from a crouch in frame 1 and walking forward along the scaffolding pipes in frames 2–5 with a brick-like object in their right hand. Meanwhile, the second person stands ~4–5 m away and below in the exterior yard (~3–4 m beyond the first person), facing and looking up toward the camera wearer while raising both hands to hold a dark pan at head level in frames 1–2 and lowering their arms to waist level in frames 3–5. Because the pose estimator outputs no keypoints at all, it provides no spatial information beyond RGB and is completely unreliable here, likely due to the steep downward egocentric viewpoint, severe back-facing self-occlusion and cropping of the foreground person's limbs, and the small pixel scale and harsh backlighting of the distant person.
